ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A certain particle moves along a straight line, and its displacement-time graph is shown in the figure. What motion does this particle make? What are the magnitude and direction of its velocity?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The particle makes uniform rectilinear motion, with velocity magnitude 0.1 m/s, in the same direction as the prescribed positive direction
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a displacement-time graph, namely the vertical axis is x/m and the horizontal axis is t/s. The graph line is a straight line slanting upward to the right, showing that the particle is at a position of about x=-0.2 m when t=0, at a position of x=0.2 m when t=4 s, and the graph line passes through x=0 at about t=2 s. Then reason: The question stem states that the particle moves along a straight line, and the x-t graph is a straight line, indicating that displacement changes uniformly with time and the slope is constant; therefore the particle makes uniform rectilinear motion. The velocity equals the slope of the x-t graph, v=Δx/Δt=[0.2-(-0.2)]/(4-0)=0.4/4=0.1 m/s. Since the graph line rises as time increases, the slope is positive, so the velocity direction is the same as the prescribed positive direction.
